title: Is there a good tool that will accept a spite sheet as a template and some model that you want to overlay onto the template that's also locally hostable?
author: Muhznit
selftext:
So I was wondering "If AI can put people in the style of a Studio Ghibli character, I wonder how it handles character template spritesheets?"

Turns out the answer is "it tries". (at least on Nano Banana 2). I scaled up the template to about 1024 px like Nano Banana outputs and gave it a prompt like "Remake the RPG Maker character sprites in this template." with some additional corrections added as I went. It's pretty good at matching the template in the sense of recoloring it and dealing with symmetrical sprites, but it still requires a bunch of manual cleanup in the end before it can be reasonably used... 

These sprites are the closest to "workable" I've gotten after several prompt corrections but even then the skirt angle is wrong, the face could use more detail, and the whole thing still animates weird. Even if you try to get it to modify the template (I tried getting the sprites to be 32x64 instead of 32x48), it struggles.

Does anyone have self-hostable solutions that work well with this technique? Or tips on how I can prepare the inputs in a better way that minimizes the manual corrections I need to make? Or tips on how to refine it even more that don't involve me paying for another subscription?

replies.author: radgh
replies.body:
Pixellab has a character tool that works this way. But their API, last I checked, did not have that functionality. You have to use it manually and Claude was unable to replicate it.

I am still waiting for the developer to reply to my $70 refund request.

Do not recommend, yet. They seriously need the character mode on the api, I would use it if I could. It still has some problems like “east attack” description given to a “war dog” = dog with a mace and sword, lol.

I used Pixel Engine instead but it’s no good. Characters change clothes between attacks and stuff lol

replies.author: Darknessborn
replies.body: The pixellab plugin for aseprite can do what you need though right? Then use the Godot aseprite integration

replies.author: radgh
replies.body: Oh maybe. I haven't heard of aseprite. I'll check it out. TY

replies.author: Darknessborn
replies.body: For any pixelart it's basically mandatory, very cool. My first game was a lot of AI art but it all needed tweaking and I did that in aseprite, now I've kinda learned it in actually doing all custom art for my second game. It's intuitive and forgiving and pixelart is easy to get good at (but hard to master)

replies.author: radgh
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/wq3d85i8vkwg1.png?width=1019&format=png&auto=webp&s=f4087fe553a96fa6a5e5e95743cd3065998eb788

So I tried PixelLab again (left) and it turned out absolutely terrible lol. I tried BitForge and the PixFlux methods. I realize aseprite is like a GUI, and that doesn't work for me. I need it to be done by Claude for this project. As an experiment it's all ai generated via prompts, no manual edits. 2nd version from SpriteCook nailed it.

Do you have any other suggestions that work with a command line workflow? Or any other services worth looking in to? SpriteCook is pretty good but the new issue is that some characters are different scales. My fighter sprite looks like a bobblehead compared to Warrior, despite being basically the same aesthetics. Although both sprites look great and similar to the reference photos.

replies.author: Darknessborn
replies.body:
Can't think of anything else cli except for the nano banana skill for Claude. If you really just want pixelart all in the same style (including specific palette-important for visual consistency) and absolutely perfect every time it's a pretty tall order. 

I used a combination of chat gpt and Gemini for [my first pixelart game](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4340400/Remember_to_Die/) but still spent about 400 hours total in aseprite fixing them up (nearly 500 images though). 

If it's an experiment then cool but if you want a successful game there's probably no avoiding some human intervention with the current tech at at least

comments.author: Char_Zulu
comments.body: might have to create the tool yourself. closest I've got is using the aesprite mcp.

comments.author: catpiss-martini
comments.body: I’m in a similar boat and there’s nothing that’ll do that seamlessly. I have been learning to make the sheets now in aseprite. Definitely don’t use pixellab. That shit was the worst
